dedupe_keys.name: global port supply chains dataset ports criticality in international trade

description: This dataset accompanies the 2022 Nature Communications article "Ports' criticality in international trade and global supply-chains". It contains the model outputs needed to reproduce the paper: the output of a modal split model, a global maritime transport network, freight flows allocated on that network, freight flow allocation through the port-to-port network, port statistics, and the links between ports and input-output tables that connect port flows to global supply chains. Coverage is global, for ports worldwide. Access: free on Mendeley Data under CC BY 4.0, published 2022-06-27, and the code of the maritime transport model and the port and supply-chain link is on GitHub; other code is available from the corresponding author on request. Caveats: the outputs are modelled estimates, not observed port-level flows, and reuse needs the article to understand the methods. It supports maritime network flow and port criticality analysis, cascading supply chain disruption studies and the prioritisation of port resilience investments, and complements the port multi-hazard risk and port systemic climate risk datasets from the same group catalogued here.
